39:Ordre de livraison : S-01a et S-02a ensemble, puis S-01b, puis S-02b. S-03 (spike) et S-04 seulement sur décision de l'utilisateur.
40-
41-### S-01a — Ne jamais arrêter DevDesk ni un processus critique, et arrêter la ligne confirmée
42-Epic : Arrêt sûr de processus — Priorité : Must — Effort : S
43-
44-En tant que développeur qui libère un port depuis l'onglet Ports, je veux que `K` refuse de toucher DevDesk, son parent direct ou le processus d'initialisation, et qu'il arrête exactement le processus que la confirmation m'a montré, afin de ne jamais tuer par erreur ma propre session, la machine ou le processus d'une autre ligne.
45-
46-Lié au bug « la confirmation relit la ligne sélectionnée au moment du Yes » (voir « Bug lié ») : cette story le corrige.
47-
48-**Critères d'acceptation**
49-1. Étant donné une ligne dont le PID est celui de DevDesk lui-même (cas réel : l'écoute d'un port-forward ou du serveur MCP), quand l'utilisateur appuie sur `K`, alors l'action est grisée avec la raison `This is DevDesk itself` (Rule 130) et aucune confirmation ne s'ouvre ; la ligne reste visible.
50-2. Étant donné une ligne dont le PID est celui du parent direct de DevDesk (seulement si ce parent est né avant DevDesk) ou le PID 1 (init sous Linux, `launchd` sous macOS), quand l'utilisateur appuie sur `K`, alors l'action est grisée avec une raison nommée : `This process started DevDesk` ou `PID 1 is the system's init process`.
51-3. Étant donné Windows et une ligne dont le PID est 0 ou 4 (System), quand l'utilisateur appuie sur `K`, alors l'action est grisée avec `Windows system process` plutôt que de laisser le système répondre « Access denied ».
52-4. Étant donné un appel direct à `ports.Kill` avec le PID de DevDesk, de son parent direct (né avant DevDesk), 1, ou 0 et 4 sous Windows (sans passer par l'interface), quand il est exécuté, alors il retourne une erreur nommant la raison et n'envoie aucun signal (garde en profondeur : l'interface n'est pas la seule protection).
53-5. Étant donné la confirmation ouverte sur la ligne `node` (PID 4242), quand le rafraîchissement du tableau change l'ordre des sockets avant que l'utilisateur réponde, alors `Yes` agit sur le PID 4242 capturé à l'ouverture et jamais sur la ligne alors sélectionnée ; le texte de la confirmation montre le nom et le PID capturés.
54-6. Étant donné la confirmation ouverte, quand l'utilisateur déplace la sélection ou que le processus disparaît du tableau rafraîchi, alors la confirmation reste sur sa cible capturée (le texte ne change pas) ; `No` ou `esc` la ferme sans signal.
55-
56:**Hors périmètre** : vérification de l'identité à chaque signal (S-01b) ; arrêt propre (S-02b) ; libellé Windows (S-02a, livré avec cette story) ; protection des autres ancêtres (terminal, `ssh`, multiplexeur) ; liste exhaustive de processus critiques (le système refuse déjà, `killFailureMessage` explique).
57-**Hypothèses** :
58-- Hypothèse: le parent direct est protégé seulement s'il est né avant DevDesk (un parent mort dont le PID a été repris par un processus plus jeune n'est pas « celui qui a lancé DevDesk »). Si l'heure de création du parent est illisible, on le protège par prudence. À valider.
59-- Hypothèse: critères 1 et 2 restent vrais sous WSL2 (identités de la VM Linux).
60-- Hypothèse: PID 0 et 4 sous Windows sont les seuls ajouts justifiés par le dépôt (PID 4 mesuré refusé dans le commentaire de `killFailureMessage`).
61-**Hypothèse retenue, non encore validée** : Q1 (seul le parent direct est refusé ; ancêtres plus hauts plus tard, avec avertissement).
62-**Questions ouvertes** : aucune bloquante.
63-
64-### S-01b — Vérifier l'identité du processus à chaque signal
65-Epic : Arrêt sûr de processus — Priorité : Must — Effort : M
66-Dépend de : S-01a (livrer S-01a d'abord ; les seams `selfPID`/`parentPID`/`procOS` et la cible capturée y sont posés).
67-
68-En tant que développeur qui libère un port, je veux que DevDesk n'envoie le signal que si le processus visé est encore celui qui était listé, afin qu'un PID réutilisé entre l'affichage et l'envoi ne fasse jamais arrêter un autre programme.
69-
70-**Critères d'acceptation**
71-1. Étant donné un rafraîchissement du tableau, quand il se termine, alors l'identité (heure de création) de chaque PID distinct qui tient un socket a été lue une seule fois et est rattachée aux lignes de ce PID (valeur brute propre à l'OS).
72-2. Étant donné une ligne listant `node` (PID 4242), quand à l'instant du signal le PID 4242 a une autre identité que celle lue au listing (processus sorti et PID repris), alors aucun signal n'est envoyé, le pied de page affiche en niveau Warn `node (PID 4242) is no longer the process that was listed — table refreshed`, et le tableau est relu.
73-3. Étant donné une ligne dont l'identité est inchangée, quand l'utilisateur confirme, alors le signal est envoyé et le comportement existant (point d'activité, message de refus du système, `PID N is no longer running`) est inchangé.
74-4. Étant donné une ligne dont l'identité n'a pas pu être lue au listing, quand l'utilisateur appuie sur `K`, alors l'action est grisée avec la raison `Cannot verify which process this is` (Rule 130), la ligne reste visible, et aucune confirmation ne s'ouvre.
75-5. Étant donné un appel direct à `ports.Kill` pour un PID dont l'identité ne peut pas être vérifiée, quand il est exécuté, alors il retourne l'erreur `Cannot verify which process PID N is — not stopped` et n'envoie aucun signal.
76-6. Étant donné Windows et l'ouverture du handle refusée (ou, en repli, la lecture refusée à l'ouverture de la confirmation), quand le signal est tenté, alors aucun signal n'est envoyé et le message dit `Refused by the system — DevDesk cannot signal PID N` (cause réelle), pas `Cannot verify`.
77-7. Étant donné la mesure du coût de lecture d'identité sous Windows (189 sockets, sans élévation), quand elle dépasse le seuil fixé dans la story (Hypothèse: à fixer par mesure avant le code ; valeur de départ proposée : 100 ms ajoutées à un rafraîchissement), alors l'identité est lue à l'ouverture de la confirmation au lieu du listing, et le critère 2 reste vrai ; la mesure et le seuil retenu sont notés dans `docs/measurements/` et `docs/architecture/network.md`.
78-
79-**Contrainte de conception (architect, décisions D-A à D-C)** : le handle est ouvert d'abord (pidfd Linux >= 5.4, handle Windows), puis l'identité est comparée sur la valeur brute propre à l'OS (ticks Linux, FILETIME Windows, `timeval` macOS), pas sur la valeur en millisecondes de gopsutil. Sans pidfd (macOS, Linux < 5.4), la fenêtre résiduelle de quelques microsecondes entre la vérification et le signal est acceptée et documentée dans `docs/architecture/network.md`.
80-**Hors périmètre** : processus protégés (S-01a) ; arrêt propre (S-02b) ; réutilisation de l'identité par un écran de processus (S-03).
81-**Hypothèses** :
82-- Hypothèse: à valider (D-D) : sous Windows, `Refused by the system` s'applique quand l'ouverture du handle est refusée au moment du signal, ou quand le repli de lecture à la confirmation est refusé. Pour les PID dont la lecture au listing est refusée (98 sur 189 sans élévation), `K` est grisé d'avance avec `Cannot verify which process this is` (critère 4) : la cause réelle (accès refusé) n'y est pas nommée. À trancher : nommer aussi la cause dans la raison grisée ?
83-- Hypothèse: les valeurs brutes ne se comparent qu'entre elles, jamais entre OS ; la valeur est opaque pour l'interface.
84-- Hypothèse: le seuil du critère 7 est un budget par rafraîchissement ; il ne change pas la cadence (2 s).
85-**Questions ouvertes** : D-D à valider par l'utilisateur ; seuil du critère 7.

87:### S-02a — Dire la vérité sous Windows : arrêt forcé direct
88-Epic : Arrêt sûr de processus — Priorité : Must — Effort : S
89-À livrer avec S-01a.
90-
91-En tant que développeur sous Windows qui arrête un processus depuis l'onglet Ports, je veux que DevDesk dise que l'arrêt est immédiat et sans sauvegarde, afin de ne jamais croire à un arrêt propre qui n'existe pas pour ce processus.
92-
93-**Critères d'acceptation**
94-1. Étant donné la confirmation ouverte sur un processus Windows (`node.exe`, PID 4412), quand l'utilisateur la lit, alors elle dit : `Terminate node.exe (PID 4412)? Windows has no clean stop for this process: it is ended at once and cannot save anything.`

97-4. Étant donné Linux ou macOS, quand S-02b n'est pas encore livrée, alors le texte et le comportement de la confirmation sont inchangés.
98-
99-**Hors périmètre** : `WM_CLOSE` (S-04) ; arrêt propre Linux et macOS (S-02b) ; changement du libellé de la touche (Q6).
100-**Hypothèses** :
101-- Hypothèse: l'arrêt propre sous Windows n'est réalisable que par `WM_CLOSE` (processus à fenêtre) ou `CTRL_BREAK` (enfant lancé par DevDesk dans un nouveau groupe) ; ni l'un ni l'autre ne s'applique à un processus arbitraire de l'onglet Ports sans fenêtre (H5 du brief). `os.Process.Signal(Interrupt)` n'est pas implémenté sous Windows en Go.
102-**Décision** : Q4 (Windows : arrêt forcé direct, libellé honnête à la première livraison).

105-### S-02b — Arrêt propre d'abord (Linux, macOS), puis forcer sur confirmation
106-Epic : Arrêt sûr de processus — Priorité : Must — Effort : M

109-En tant que développeur qui arrête un serveur de dev ou une base locale depuis l'onglet Ports sous Linux ou macOS, je veux qu'un arrêt propre soit tenté d'abord, puis qu'on me propose de forcer, afin de ne pas perdre de données par un arrêt brutal inutile, sans que l'interface se fige pendant l'attente.

111-**Critères d'acceptation**
112-1. Étant donné la confirmation ouverte sur `nginx` (PID 812), quand l'utilisateur la lit, alors elle annonce un arrêt propre en deux temps : `Ask nginx (PID 812) to stop?` suivi de `Sends SIGTERM and waits up to 5 s. You can force it afterwards.` ; elle n'annonce plus un SIGKILL.

It gets no chance to shut down cleanly.` ; refuser laisse le processus en l'état sans nouveau signal ; confirmer envoie SIGKILL ; jamais de SIGKILL sans cette confirmation.

Étant donné l'attente en cours, quand l'utilisateur appuie sur `esc`, alors l'attente s'arrête (le SIGTERM déjà envoyé n'est pas rappelé), le pied de page dit `Stopped waiting for nginx (812) — the stop request was already sent`, et un tick de sonde arrivé après `esc` est ignoré (génération périmée) ; pendant toute l'attente, le tableau continue de se rafraîchir et les touches répondent.

39	// statusLine is what the Ports tab derives on every frame. Pausing is a state
40	// rather than an event, so it is rendered from pm.paused instead of set as a
41	// message — a message would expire after three seconds while still paused.
42	func (pm *PortsModel) statusLine() components.Status {
43		// The selected row says what is happening to it, before the tab's own state.
44		st := components.Status{Detail: pm.rowDetail()}
45		// Staleness outranks the pause: a pause is what the user asked for, an
46		// unreachable Docker is not, and only one of the two makes the rows lie.
47		if pm.stale {
48			st.Text, st.Level = pm.staleLabel(), components.LevelError
49		} else if pm.paused {
50			st.Text = "Paused — press space to resume"
51		}

56	// its PID, and nothing otherwise (this view remembers no failure).

58		entry, ok := pm.table.Selected()

98		// existed only to avoid recreating the table on every two-second tick and
99		// losing the scroll position; SetItems guarantees that instead.

126		// (Rule 128), and what was left was a table refreshing into failure with

149	// activity column: the query used to run against all six joined, and it still
150	// does. Column 0 is the activity dot (Rule 125); a busy PID is Running there.
151	func portsColumns() []datatable.Column[ports.Socket] {
152		text := func(sizing datatable.Sizing, get func(ports.Socket) string) datatable.Column[ports.Socket] {
153			return datatable.Column[ports.Socket]{Sizing: sizing, Cell: get, Search: get}
154		}

156		// §3.45 in one table: they used to sit at a declared 26 whatever the
157		// terminal was, cutting "[2606:2800:220:1:248:1893:25c8:1946]:443" in half
158		// at 200 columns while Process took 110 cells for "svchost.exe".
159		proto := text(datatable.SizingFixed, func(p ports.Socket) string { return p.Protocol })
160		state := text(datatable.SizingFixed, func(p ports.Socket) string { return p.State })

199	// them. `numeric` and `paused` are shown in the bar but filter nothing — they
200	// report a mode, which is why they are not consulted here.
201	func matchPortTokens(p ports.Socket, active map[string]bool) bool {
202		return matchesActive(p.Protocol, active, filterTokenTCP, filterTokenUDP) &&
203			matchesActive(p.State, active, filterTokenListen, filterTokenEstab)

207	// on. A group with nothing on does not filter: that is "no opinion", not
208	// "match nothing", and getting the two confused would empty the table on open.
209	func matchesActive(value string, active map[string]bool, labels ...string) bool {
210		anyOn := false
211		for _, label := range labels {
212			if !active[label] {
213				continue
214			}
215			anyOn = true
216			if strings.EqualFold(value, label) {
217				return true
218			}
219		}
220		return !anyOn

233					{Label: filterTokenUDP},
234					{Label: filterTokenListen},
235					{Label: filterTokenEstab},
236					{Label: filterTokenNumeric},
237					{Label: filterTokenPaused},
238				},

240				// A PID, not a socket: killing a process takes every socket it
241				// holds, so every one of its rows spins together — which is what

262		pm.height = height

271	func (pm *PortsModel) update(msg tea.Msg) (*PortsModel, tea.Cmd) {
272		switch msg := msg.(type) {
273		case portsTickMsg:
274			return pm.handleTick()
275		case shared.TerminalFocusMsg:
276			return pm.setTerminalFocus(msg)
277		case portsDataMsg:
278			return pm.handleData(msg)
279		case portsKillResultMsg:
280			return pm.handleKillResult(msg)
281		case components.ConfirmModalYesMsg:
282			pm.confirmModal = nil
283			return pm.killSelected()
284		case components.ConfirmModalNoMsg:
285			pm.confirmModal = nil
286			return pm, nil
287		case tea.KeyPressMsg:
288			return pm.handleKey(msg)
289		case tea.PasteMsg:
290			return pm.handlePaste(msg)
291		}
292		return pm, nil
293	}

295	func (pm *PortsModel) handleTick() (*PortsModel, tea.Cmd) {
296		if pm.paused || pm.unfocused {
297			return pm, portsTickCmd(pm.refresh)
298		}
299		return pm, tea.Batch(fetchPortsCmd(pm.numericAddrs), portsTickCmd(pm.refresh))
300	}
301	
302	// setTerminalFocus records the focus. On the edge after a blur it reads once,
303	// with no new tick (the chain kept running), unless the user paused the poll.
304	func (pm *PortsModel) setTerminalFocus(msg shared.TerminalFocusMsg) (*PortsModel, tea.Cmd) {
305		pm.unfocused = !msg.Focused
306		if msg.Focused && msg.Resume && !pm.paused {
307			return pm, fetchPortsCmd(pm.numericAddrs)
308		}
309		return pm, nil
310	}
311	
312	func (pm *PortsModel) handleData(msg portsDataMsg) (*PortsModel, tea.Cmd) {
313		if msg.err != nil {
314			log.Printf("ERROR [netdiag/ports] ports.List: %v", msg.err)
315			// The rows stay: they are dated, not wrong, and the status line is what
316			// says so. No footer message — this is a state, and a state that
317			// expires after three seconds is how a dead table came to look alive.
318			pm.stale = true
319			return pm, nil
320		}
321		pm.stale = false
322		pm.lastOK = time.Now()
323		// The cursor and the scroll survive this, which is what the whole
324		// tableReady dance existed to achieve on a two-second tick.
325		pm.table.SetItems(msg.ports)
326		return pm, nil
327	}
328	
329	func (pm *PortsModel) handleKillResult(msg portsKillResultMsg) (*PortsModel, tea.Cmd) {
330		// On every outcome: a kill that failed has to let the socket state show
331		// again rather than go on turning.
332		pm.table.ClearBusy(msg.pid)
333		if msg.err != nil {
334			log.Printf("ERROR [netdiag/ports] ports.Kill pid=%s: %v", msg.pid, msg.err)
335			return pm, pm.footer.Error(killFailureMessage(msg.pid, msg.err))
336		}
337		return pm, pm.footer.Info(fmt.Sprintf("Process %s terminated", msg.pid))
338	}
339	
340	// killFailureMessage says why the signal did not land.
341	//
342	// DevDesk signals with the rights it has (§3.43), so the refusal the user meets
343	// most often is the operating system's — another user's process, a service, one
344	// Windows protects. "Failed to kill PID 1234" gave them no reason to suspect
345	// that, and made "access denied" and "already gone" the same sentence.
346	//
347	// The platform error itself never reaches the screen: it comes back in the
348	// machine's own language — measured here, PID 4 answers `OpenProcess: Accès
349	// refusé.` — which is the route stage's rule (§3.44). errors.Is reads through
350	// the %w wrapping ports.Kill applies, and both sentinels are the standard
351	// library's.
352	//
353	// The permission branch was measured on Windows: killing PID 4 (System) gives
354	// ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED, which syscall.Errno maps onto os.ErrPermission. EPERM
355	// maps the same way on Unix.
356	//
357	// **The "already gone" branch does not fire on Windows**, and that is measured
358	// too: a PID that does not exist fails OpenProcess with
359	// ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER, which maps to neither sentinel, so it falls to the
360	// generic message. Mapping that code would be a guess — it is what an invalid
361	// argument returns as well — and the row disappears on the next two-second
362	// refresh anyway. The branch is kept because ESRCH does map to
363	// os.ErrProcessDone on Unix.
364	func killFailureMessage(pid string, err error) string {
365		switch {
366		case errors.Is(err, os.ErrPermission):
367			return fmt.Sprintf("Refused by the system — DevDesk cannot signal PID %s", pid)
368		case errors.Is(err, os.ErrProcessDone):
369			return fmt.Sprintf("PID %s is no longer running", pid)
370		}
371		return fmt.Sprintf("Failed to kill PID %s — check logs", pid)
372	}

374	func (pm *PortsModel) handleKey(msg tea.KeyPressMsg) (*PortsModel, tea.Cmd) {
375		if pm.confirmModal != nil {
376			var cmd tea.Cmd
377			pm.confirmModal, cmd = pm.confirmModal.Update(msg)
378			return pm, cmd
379		}
380		if pm.table.InEditMode() {
381			cmd := pm.table.Update(msg)
382			pm.table.GotoTop() // a narrowing query starts from the first match
383			return pm, cmd
384		}
385		return pm.handleKeyNormal(msg)
386	}

388	// handlePaste gives pasted text to the filter bar while it has the keyboard and
389	// no modal is open; otherwise it is dropped (Rule 111).
390	func (pm *PortsModel) handlePaste(msg tea.PasteMsg) (*PortsModel, tea.Cmd) {
391		if pm.confirmModal != nil || !pm.table.InEditMode() {
392			return pm, nil
393		}
394		cmd := pm.table.Update(msg)
395		pm.table.GotoTop() // a narrowing query starts from the first match
396		return pm, cmd
397	}

399	// toggleToken flips a filter and returns to the top, since the list under the
400	// cursor is not the list the user was looking at any more.
401	func (pm *PortsModel) toggleToken(label string) {
402		pm.table.SetTokenActive(label, !pm.table.IsTokenActive(label))
403		pm.table.GotoTop()
404	}
405	
406	func (pm *PortsModel) handleKeyNormal(msg tea.KeyPressMsg) (*PortsModel, tea.Cmd) {
407		switch msg.String() {
408		case "up", "down", "pgup", "pgdown", "home", "end", "/":
409			return pm, pm.table.Update(msg)
410		case keymap.Space:
411			pm.paused = !pm.paused
412			pm.table.SetTokenActive(filterTokenPaused, pm.paused)
413			// Pausing is a state, not an event: it is derived in statusLine rather
414			// than set as a message, which would expire while still paused.
415		case "t":
416			pm.toggleToken(filterTokenTCP)
417		case "u":
418			pm.toggleToken(filterTokenUDP)
419		case "l":
420			pm.toggleToken(filterTokenListen)
421		case "e":
422			pm.toggleToken(filterTokenEstab)
423		case "n":
424			pm.numericAddrs = !pm.numericAddrs
425			pm.table.SetTokenActive(filterTokenNumeric, pm.numericAddrs)
426			return pm, fetchPortsCmd(pm.numericAddrs)
427		case "z":
428			for _, label := range []string{
429				filterTokenTCP, filterTokenUDP, filterTokenListen, filterTokenEstab, filterTokenPaused,
430			} {
431				pm.table.SetTokenActive(label, false)
432			}
433			pm.table.FilterBar().ClearSearch()
434			pm.table.SetItems(pm.table.Items()) // re-apply with the query gone
435			pm.paused = false
436			pm.table.GotoTop()
437		case keymap.Kill:
438			return pm.confirmKill()
439		}
440		return pm, nil
441	}
442	
443	// confirmKill asks before sending the signal.
444	//
445	// This is the one action in the application that reaches outside it: not a
446	// container to be brought back up, but a process belonging to whoever is at
447	// this machine, killed with SIGKILL so it gets no chance to save anything. It
448	// had no confirmation at all, while deleting a container — recreatable from its
449	// image — had one (§3.26).
450	func (pm *PortsModel) confirmKill() (*PortsModel, tea.Cmd) {
451		if k := pm.killable(); !k.Enabled() {
452			return pm, pm.footer.Warn(k.Reason)
453		}
454		entry, _ := pm.table.Selected()
455		if pm.table.IsBusy(entry.PID) {
456			return pm, pm.footer.Warn("Already killing PID " + entry.PID)
457		}
458		pm.confirmModal = components.NewConfirmModal(
459			"Kill Process",
460			fmt.Sprintf("Send SIGKILL to %s (PID %s)?\n\nThe process gets no chance to shut down cleanly.",
461				entry.Process, entry.PID),
462		)
463		return pm, nil
464	}
465	
466	// Why K does not apply, written once so the header, the footer and the tests
467	// cannot drift apart on the wording (Rule 129 — English US).
468	const (
469		reasonNoSocketRow = "No socket selected"
470		reasonNoPID       = "The system did not say which process holds this socket"
471	)
472	
473	// killable reports whether K has a process to signal (Rule 130).
474	//
475	// A socket the system declines to attribute carries no PID — `List` blanks a
476	// PID of zero rather than printing it, because process 0 is a whole process
477	// group on Unix and a row reading "0" would look killable. That is the state
478	// this greys; whether the operating system will *accept* the signal is a
479	// different question, and one only the attempt can answer.
480	func (pm *PortsModel) killable() shortcut.Availability {
481		entry, ok := pm.table.Selected()
482		switch {
483		case !ok:
484			return shortcut.Unavailable(reasonNoSocketRow)
485		case entry.PID == "":
486			return shortcut.Unavailable(reasonNoPID)
487		}
488		return shortcut.Availability{}
489	}
490	
491	// killSelected sends the signal, once confirmed.
492	func (pm *PortsModel) killSelected() (*PortsModel, tea.Cmd) {
493		entry, ok := pm.table.Selected()
494		if !ok {
495			return pm, nil
496		}
497		if entry.PID == "" || pm.table.IsBusy(entry.PID) {
498			return pm, nil
499		}
500		// Keyed on the PID, so every socket the process holds shows the running dot
501		// at once — which is what happens: the kill takes them all. The table reads
502		// the busy mark at render; the router's frame drives the blink.
503		pm.table.MarkBusy(entry.PID, "Killing "+entry.Process+" ("+entry.PID+")")
504		return pm, killProcessCmd(entry.PID)
505	}
506	
507	// view renders the table. An empty table stays a table (Rule 139) — its
508	// header and no rows — whether it is genuinely empty, filtered down to
509	// nothing, still loading, or stale: those are a footer status (statusLine) and
510	// a header count, never body text.
511	func (pm *PortsModel) view() string {
512		return pm.table.View()
513	}
514	
515	// summaryLine counts what is on screen, for the header (Rule 139).
516	func (pm *PortsModel) summaryLine() string {
517		return fmt.Sprintf("%d", len(pm.table.Items()))
518	}

Étant donné une ligne dont le PID est celui de DevDesk lui-même (cas réel : l'écoute d'un port-forward ou du serveur MCP), quand l'utilisateur appuie sur `K`, alors l'action est grisée avec la raison `This is DevDesk itself` (Rule 130) et aucune confirmation ne s'ouvre ; la ligne reste visible.

51-3. Étant donné Windows et une ligne dont le PID est 0 ou 4 (System), quand l'utilisateur appuie sur `K`, alors l'action est grisée avec `Windows system process` plutôt que de laisser le système répondre « Access denied ».

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP; a Proxy row says whether a proxy variable applies, the checks themselves stay direct, DEVDESK-582) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only) + a path trace under Diagnostics (Trace Path button, or `H` on the route row; no separate tab since DEVDESK-471) (native path trace, on native Linux, native Windows (IPv4 only, ICMP echoes through `iphlpapi`, DEVDESK-486) and WSL2: on macOS and WSL1 the button, `H`, `enter` and `ctrl+o` are greyed and the footer says why, DEVDESK-334; the column starts with this machine, its interface and its gateway; `ctrl+o` can start it from a running Docker Engine container instead (container and network rows, hops still traced from this machine); `H` on the Diagnostics route row opens the trace level on that host without starting it (greyed with the reason on an unsupported platform or a target the trace refuses; its interface and gateway rows reuse the Local route check's reading of the same address, read once, DEVDESK-473), and in the trace level `enter` starts or restarts it, `ctrl+o` picks the source, `esc` cancels then goes back where it came from; under WSL2 the source row says `WSL2 (VM), not the Windows host` with the networking mode, and in NAT mode the gateway and TTL 1 hop are tagged `Windows host (virtual switch)` only when proven, DEVDESK-333; the interface row says `no route` when the kernel proves there is none and `undetermined` when the routing table could not be read, a no-route error keeps the local rows, a trace that ends on the hop limit or the deadline folds its silent tail into one `silent` row and marks the `last to answer` hop, and the target refuses a `:port`, DEVDESK-335)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, when its transcript is gone, or while the terminal is not focused (header `Updates › paused`, then `paused (terminal not focused)`; `app.when_unfocused: run` keeps it live); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. ## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go
mise run ci           # the five checks in order (fmt-check, vet, lint, build, test-race), stops at the first failure; unlike check it rewrites no file and also runs build and test-race. `test-race` is the only test run (`-race` covers `go test`); `mise run test` stays available alone for the fast local loop. CI runs fmt-check, vet, lint and build in the `Lint and build` job and `test-race` in the `Test` job, on every pull request, docs-only ones included (the docs-only shortcut applies to `Lint and build` only); the whole CI targets under 10 minutes, so run this locally before a PR to catch a red check early

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Nexus tests replay recorded fixtures (DEVDESK-511, DEVDESK-580).** Three campaigns
in `internal/nexusfixture/fixtures/` (`catalog`, `cachedonly`, `access`) replay through
`fakenexus`: `mise run test` needs no bench, cluster or secret. A `record: pending` file is never
versioned (`TestNoPendingFixtureIsVersioned`); `DEVDESK_FIXTURE_RECORDING=1` only in a local recording session.
`nexus-bench record` without `--state` applies no state filter and can overwrite an `upstream-cut` fixture.
Bench writes go only through `nexus-bench:*` tasks and the guarded `DEVDESK_NEXUS_BENCH_SCENARIOS=1` test.
Dated measures live in `docs/measurements/`; a measure contradicting a criterion or the code is frozen and noted, never fixed in the same PR.

**Scanner containers and the proxy (DEVDESK-583, D164).** Every `run --rm` a scanner
issues goes through `containerRun{…}.cmd()` (`internal/scan/container_run.go`): the proxy
variables travel as `-e NAME` with the value in the child environment, never in argv. The
guard `TestContainerGuard*` (`internal/netproxy/container_guard_test.go`) fails on any other
`"run"` literal; only the two permanent exceptions in that file are allowed. The tests of
`internal/scan`, `internal/app` and `internal/ui/security` neutralise the seams
`proxyForward` / `containerForward` in their `TestMain`, so a developer's `HTTPS_PROXY` does not
change an exact argv. The `TestMain` of `internal/app`
also replaces `detectTools` (`internal/app/scan_tools.go`, production value `scan.Detect`) with an
empty report, so `App.Init` never runs the `trivy`, `gitleaks` and `plumber` of the machine
(DEVDESK-645); `TestInitDoesNotRunTheScannersOfTheHost` and `TestDetectToolsIsScanDetectInProduction`
guard it.

**Tests and the host secret store (DEVDESK-610).** By default `credentials.Select` and
`KeyringAvailable` reach the real keyring of the machine (Secret Service over D-Bus on
Linux); a locked keyring blocks the whole suite until the timeout. A test binary that can
reach them isolates the store: `fakekeyring.Install()` in `TestMain`, then
`fakekeyring.Fresh(t)` (or `FreshUnreachable(t, err)` for a locked keyring) per test, from
`internal/testutil/fakekeyring`. `isolateHome(t)` already calls `Fresh` in `internal/app` and
`internal/ui/setup`. Two guards enforce it: at run time, any keyring or `git credential` call
in a test binary without the fake panics with `DEVDESK-610` and the operation; statically,
`TestHostStoreGuard*` (`internal/credentials/hoststore_guard_test.go`) fails on K1 (go-keyring
imported outside `internal/credentials`), K2 (`SwapHostStoreForTest` in non-test code) and K3
(`fakekeyring` imported by non-test code). The seam is `credentials.HostStore` and
`SwapHostStoreForTest`, reserved for tests (it panics outside a test binary). Limits: the
runtime guard only sees the paths a test runs; the static one misses an aliased package
name, a dynamic import and an external binary; `gitHelperUsable` reads the git config
unguarded; `Install` and `Fresh` are global, so no `t.Parallel`. See
`docs/architecture/configuration.md`, "Testing code that reaches the secret store".

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update
handlers switch on `tea.KeyPressMsg`, never the `tea.KeyMsg` interface (it also
matches releases). A paste is a `tea.PasteMsg`, not a key (Rule 111). Guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`,
`viewport_keymap_scan_test.go`) fail the suite otherwise; limits are listed in
`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

## Dependencies

Go 1.27 (`go 1.27.3` in `go.mod`). Key libraries (versions as in `go.mod`):
- `charm.land/bubbletea/v2` (v2.1.1) - TUI framework (v2: `tea.KeyPressMsg`, `tea.PasteMsg`, `View() tea.View`)
- `charm.land/bubbles/v2` (v2.2.1) - Pre-built TUI components (table, textinput, viewport)
- `charm.land/lipgloss/v2` (v2.0.6) - Styling (no global colour profile; colours are `image/color.Color`)
- `github.com/charmbracelet/colorprofile` (v0.4.3) - colour profile `main.go` forces under Windows Terminal (replaces `termenv`)
- `github.com/NimbleMarkets/ntcharts/v2` (v2.9.0) - dashboard sparkline
- `github.com/charmbracelet/x/ansi` - ANSI-safe width, strip and cut
- `gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go` - GitLab API client
- `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing` - ICMP ping functionality (maintained fork of go-ping/ping)
- `github.com/google/go-github/v68` - GitHub API client (§3.6)
- `github.com/libp2p/go-netroute` - which interface a destination leaves by, on all three platforms (§3.44)
- `golang.org/x/sys` - direct (Rule 303): the socket calls of `internal/nettrace` (`IP_TTL`, `IP_RECVERR`, `recvmsg` on the error queue); `x/sys/windows` serves `iphlpapi` (the Windows path trace, `IcmpSendEcho2`)
- `github.com/zalando/go-keyring` - host secret manager (wincred / Keychain / Secret Service), no cgo
- `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` - YAML configuration

## Code Conventions

- Comments: **English only** (Rule 307) — existing French comments are not rewritten wholesale, but any new or edited comment is in English
- Commit messages: **English only** (Rule 307)
- UI text and logs: **English US only** (Rule 129)
- Bubbletea models define their own message types
- Use `theme` package for consistent styling (`internal/ui/theme/`)
- Config changes must call `config.Save()` to persist
- All colors defined in `theme/colors.go`, all styles in `theme/styles.go`
- Message naming: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg` (e.g., `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`)
- Context names: the rule exists twice (`config.ValidateContextName`, `contextcmd.ValidName`); change both or neither (`TestContextNameRulesAgree`). Creation refuses `-`, `new`, `list` (`config.ValidateNewContextName`); loading does not (D91)

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`
- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`

**Views render through `Render()`** (Bubble Tea v2): a top-level view implements
`Render() string` and `View() tea.View { return tea.NewView(m.Render()) }`; only the
router (`App.View()`) sets terminal state such as `AltScreen` and `BackgroundColor`. Components keep
`View() string`. Colours are `color.Color`; hex literals stay in `theme/colors.go`.

**Update() case extraction**: If a case block exceeds 5 lines, extract to `handle[MessageType]()` method returning `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

```bash
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go
mise run ci           # the five checks in order (fmt-check, vet, lint, build, test-race), stops at the first failure; unlike check it rewrites no file and also runs build and test-race. `test-race` is the only test run (`-race` covers `go test`); `mise run test` stays available alone for the fast local loop. CI runs fmt-check, vet, lint and build in the `Lint and build` job and `test-race` in the `Test` job, on every pull request, docs-only ones included (the docs-only shortcut applies to `Lint and build` only); the whole CI targets under 10 minutes, so run this locally before a PR to catch a red check early

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

## Architecture

The deep notes live in `docs/architecture/`, one file per area, and they are
**not** `@`-imported: an `@` would inline all of it into every session, which is
the thing this split exists to avoid. Read the file that covers what you are
touching, and update it in the same commit as the code.

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Nexus tests replay recorded fixtures (DEVDESK-511, DEVDESK-580).** Three campaigns
in `internal/nexusfixture/fixtures/` (`catalog`, `cachedonly`, `access`) replay through
`fakenexus`: `mise run test` needs no bench, cluster or secret. A `record: pending` file is never
versioned (`TestNoPendingFixtureIsVersioned`); `DEVDESK_FIXTURE_RECORDING=1` only in a local recording session.
`nexus-bench record` without `--state` applies no state filter and can overwrite an `upstream-cut` fixture.
Bench writes go only through `nexus-bench:*` tasks and the guarded `DEVDESK_NEXUS_BENCH_SCENARIOS=1` test.
Dated measures live in `docs/measurements/`; a measure contradicting a criterion or the code is frozen and noted, never fixed in the same PR.

**Scanner containers and the proxy (DEVDESK-583, D164).** Every `run --rm` a scanner
issues goes through `containerRun{…}.cmd()` (`internal/scan/container_run.go`): the proxy
variables travel as `-e NAME` with the value in the child environment, never in argv. The
guard `TestContainerGuard*` (`internal/netproxy/container_guard_test.go`) fails on any other
`"run"` literal; only the two permanent exceptions in that file are allowed. The tests of
`internal/scan`, `internal/app` and `internal/ui/security` neutralise the seams
`proxyForward` / `containerForward` in their `TestMain`, so a developer's `HTTPS_PROXY` does not
change an exact argv. The `TestMain` of `internal/app`
also replaces `detectTools` (`internal/app/scan_tools.go`, production value `scan.Detect`) with an
empty report, so `App.Init` never runs the `trivy`, `gitleaks` and `plumber` of the machine
(DEVDESK-645); `TestInitDoesNotRunTheScannersOfTheHost` and `TestDetectToolsIsScanDetectInProduction`
guard it.

**Tests and the host secret store (DEVDESK-610).** By default `credentials.Select` and
`KeyringAvailable` reach the real keyring of the machine (Secret Service over D-Bus on
Linux); a locked keyring blocks the whole suite until the timeout. A test binary that can
reach them isolates the store: `fakekeyring.Install()` in `TestMain`, then
`fakekeyring.Fresh(t)` (or `FreshUnreachable(t, err)` for a locked keyring) per test, from
`internal/testutil/fakekeyring`. `isolateHome(t)` already calls `Fresh` in `internal/app` and
`internal/ui/setup`. Two guards enforce it: at run time, any keyring or `git credential` call
in a test binary without the fake panics with `DEVDESK-610` and the operation; statically,
`TestHostStoreGuard*` (`internal/credentials/hoststore_guard_test.go`) fails on K1 (go-keyring
imported outside `internal/credentials`), K2 (`SwapHostStoreForTest` in non-test code) and K3
(`fakekeyring` imported by non-test code). The seam is `credentials.HostStore` and
`SwapHostStoreForTest`, reserved for tests (it panics outside a test binary). Limits: the
runtime guard only sees the paths a test runs; the static one misses an aliased package
name, a dynamic import and an external binary; `gitHelperUsable` reads the git config
unguarded; `Install` and `Fresh` are global, so no `t.Parallel`. See
`docs/architecture/configuration.md`, "Testing code that reaches the secret store".

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update
handlers switch on `tea.KeyPressMsg`, never the `tea.KeyMsg` interface (it also
matches releases). A paste is a `tea.PasteMsg`, not a key (Rule 111). Guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`,
`viewport_keymap_scan_test.go`) fail the suite otherwise; limits are listed in
`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

## Dependencies

Go 1.27 (`go 1.27.3` in `go.mod`). Key libraries (versions as in `go.mod`):
- `charm.land/bubbletea/v2` (v2.1.1) - TUI framework (v2: `tea.KeyPressMsg`, `tea.PasteMsg`, `View() tea.View`)
- `charm.land/bubbles/v2` (v2.2.1) - Pre-built TUI components (table, textinput, viewport)
- `charm.land/lipgloss/v2` (v2.0.6) - Styling (no global colour profile; colours are `image/color.Color`)
- `github.com/charmbracelet/colorprofile` (v0.4.3) - colour profile `main.go` forces under Windows Terminal (replaces `termenv`)
- `github.com/NimbleMarkets/ntcharts/v2` (v2.9.0) - dashboard sparkline
- `github.com/charmbracelet/x/ansi` - ANSI-safe width, strip and cut
- `gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go` - GitLab API client
- `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing` - ICMP ping functionality (maintained fork of go-ping/ping)
- `github.com/google/go-github/v68` - GitHub API client (§3.6)
- `github.com/libp2p/go-netroute` - which interface a destination leaves by, on all three platforms (§3.44)
- `golang.org/x/sys` - direct (Rule 303): the socket calls of `internal/nettrace` (`IP_TTL`, `IP_RECVERR`, `recvmsg` on the error queue); `x/sys/windows` serves `iphlpapi` (the Windows path trace, `IcmpSendEcho2`)
- `github.com/zalando/go-keyring` - host secret manager (wincred / Keychain / Secret Service), no cgo
- `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` - YAML configuration

## Code Conventions

- Comments: **English only** (Rule 307) — existing French comments are not rewritten wholesale, but any new or edited comment is in English
- Commit messages: **English only** (Rule 307)
- UI text and logs: **English US only** (Rule 129)
- Bubbletea models define their own message types
- Use `theme` package for consistent styling (`internal/ui/theme/`)
- Config changes must call `config.Save()` to persist
- All colors defined in `theme/colors.go`, all styles in `theme/styles.go`
- Message naming: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg` (e.g., `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`)
- Context names: the rule exists twice (`config.ValidateContextName`, `contextcmd.ValidName`); change both or neither (`TestContextNameRulesAgree`). Creation refuses `-`, `new`, `list` (`config.ValidateNewContextName`); loading does not (D91)

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`
- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`

**Views render through `Render()`** (Bubble Tea v2): a top-level view implements
`Render() string` and `View() tea.View { return tea.NewView(m.Render()) }`; only the
router (`App.View()`) sets terminal state such as `AltScreen` and `BackgroundColor`. Components keep
`View() string`. Colours are `color.Color`; hex literals stay in `theme/colors.go`.

**Update() case extraction**: If a case block exceeds 5 lines, extract to `handle[MessageType]()` method returning `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

</system-reminder>

# TUI — Rule index

TUI rules are split across 5 topic files:

| File | Rules | Content |
|---------|--------|---------|
| [`tui-layout.md`](tui-layout.md) | 101, 107, 108, 111, 112, 123, 124, 130, 134, 137, 138 | General layout, keybindings, viewport, tabs, shortcuts header, format descriptions, shortcuts obviousness |
| [`tui-theme.md`](tui-theme.md) | 102, 105, 115, 117, 118, 119, 127, 129 | Colors, lipgloss background, `theme.*` helpers, language |
| [`tui-forms.md`](tui-forms.md) | 103, 104, 113, 114, 120, 121, 131, 132, 133, 135, 140 | Forms, modals, focus, status icons, value cycling, WrappedInput, key assignment, invalid field |
| [`tui-tables.md`](tui-tables.md) | 106, 116, 122, 125, 136, 139 | Tables, column widths, plain-text cells + color via `Style`, filter bar, body never replaced (loading or message) |
| [`tui-behavior.md`](tui-behavior.md) | 109, 110, 126, 128 | Bubble Tea (Cmd/Update), scan cache, footer messages (three levels, one component) |

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer, never in the body: with the shared activity dot (`Status.Activity`, `●`/`○`, `SetBlinkPhase`), for a view's own load as well as for work the router tracks. The braille spinner API is removed (DEVDESK-377): nothing under `internal/` imports `bubbles/v2/spinner` or names `Status.Spinner`, `SetSpinnerFrame`, `theme.SpinnerMessage` or `theme.SpinnerStyle` (`TestNoViewImportsTheBubblesSpinner`, `TestRemovedSpinnerSymbolsStayGone`), with no exception. A new `Activity` value not driven by the jobs registry must implement `WantsBlink()`, or the dot stays fixed.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a loading screen or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 140** — An invalid form field is underlined through `theme.StyleInvalidField` (the only entry point to the underline API), and the error is also in the footer at level Error, derived on every render. The underline is never the only carrier.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

# Planning Rules

# TUI — Bubble Tea behavior & architecture

### Rule 109 : Bubble Tea message naming convention

- Format: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg`
- Examples: `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`, `ConfirmModalYesMsg`
- Always document with a comment
- Group related messages together in the file

### Rule 110 : NEVER modify the model inside a Cmd ⚠️

**Fundamental principle of Bubble Tea (Elm architecture).**

`Update()`, `View()`, and `Cmd`s execute in parallel. Modifying the model inside a Cmd creates race conditions detectable with `go run -race`.

| Component | Role | Can modify the model? |
|-----------|------|---------------------------|
| `Update()` | Processes messages | ✅ YES (the only allowed place) |
| `View()` | Renders the UI | ❌ NO (read-only) |
| `Cmd` | Async I/O operations | ❌ NO (returns messages) |

```go
// ❌ WRONG — race condition
func (m *Model) logout() tea.Cmd {
    return func() tea.Msg {
        m.authenticated = false  // DANGER
        return nil
    }
}

// ✅ CORRECT — message + Update()
type LogoutCompleteMsg struct{}

func (m *Model) logout() tea.Cmd {
    url := m.urlInput.Value()  // copy the data we need
    return func() tea.Msg {
        auth := gitlabpkg.NewAuth(m.storage)
        _ = auth.Logout(url)
        return LogoutCompleteMsg{}
    }
}

case LogoutCompleteMsg:
    m.authenticated = false  // thread-safe inside Update()
    m.user = nil
    return m, nil
```

**Golden rule**: Cmds do the "dirty work" (I/O), then send a message to `Update()`.

### Rule 126 : Scan cache behavior (Images & Workspaces)

| Action | Disk cache | Memory cache | Scan triggered |
|--------|-------------|---------------|------------|
| `Enter` (scanned item) | Read | Read | No |
| `Enter` (not scanned) | — | — | No |
| `ctrl+s` (in progress) | Blocked | Blocked | No |
| `ctrl+s` (available) | Overwritten | Updated | Yes (item only) |
| `A` (unscanned) | Unchanged | Unchanged | Yes (unscanned) |
| `ctrl+a` (all) | **Purged** | **Purged** | Yes (all) |

**`ctrl+a` must clear the cache before relaunching the scans:**
```go
// ✅ CORRECT
func (m Model) requestScanAll() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
    var keys []string
    for _, img := range m.images {
        delete(m.scanCache, name)  // in-memory purge inside Update()
        keys = append(keys, name)
    }
    return m, tea.Batch(deleteScanCacheCmd(keys), batchScanCmd(keys, m.defaultScanOpts()))
}
```

### Rule 128 : Footer messages — three levels, centered, one component

**`components.FooterMessage` is the only implementation.** A view does not
render its own message: it declares one, sets it from `Update()`, and
renders it via `m.footer.View(width, status)`.

There used to be eight of them, one per view, each with its own fields,
timer, and lipgloss block. That is what produced the flaw this component
removes: nobody ever centered the error branch, in any of the eight, so
errors were left-aligned everywhere while notices were centered.

#### The three levels

They are defined by **what happened**, not by how it feels:

| Level | Meaning | Color |
|--------|------|---------|
| `Error` | an operation failed, or the system refused it | `ColorFooterError` = the red of **CRITICAL** CVEs |
| `Warn` | the action cannot be honored as requested, but nothing failed: an unmet precondition, already in progress, not applicable here | `ColorFooterWarn` = the orange of **MEDIUM** CVEs |
| `Info` | a neutral fact, or a successful operation | `ColorFooterInfo` = `ColorText`, the ordinary text color |

Info is not bold, the other two are: the hierarchy runs through weight as
much as through hue, and a neutral info in bold would turn back into an
alert.

The colors are **semantic aliases** assigned in `ApplyTheme` (`colors.go`),
like the viewer's syntax colors: no theme file gains a key. They target the
**severity** names rather than `ColorError` / `ColorWarn` — the default
theme makes them coincide, so the choice is invisible today; it stops being
invisible in a theme that separates them.

#### What is forbidden

- ❌ `theme.StatusErrorStyle`, `StatusOKStyle`, `StatusWarningStyle`, or
  `ColorHighlight` inside a `RenderFooter`, a `renderInfoLine`, or a
  `renderInfoText` — `TestNoViewStylesItsOwnFooterMessage` scans the sources
  and fails, naming the file, line, and function.
- ❌ **Green** in a footer. It is reserved for status icons (Rule 121).
- ❌ A **left-aligned** message. `View` centers, always, across the full
  width.
- ❌ A local timer (`clearFooterCmd`, `clearInfoMsgCmd`, …): the component
  carries it.

#### Mandatory pattern

```go
// 1. The model declares a field.
type Model struct {
    footer sharedcomponents.FooterMessage
}

// 2. Update() sets the message and returns its timer. A message set without
//    its timer never disappears.
case SomeErrorMsg:
    log.Printf("ERROR [package/view] action: %v", msg.Err)
    return m, m.footer.Error("Failed to load data — check logs")

case ScanAlreadyRunningMsg:
    return m, m.footer.Warn("Scan already in progress")

// 3. Update() offers unhandled messages to the component, which consumes
//    the expiry addressed to it.
m.footer.Handle(msg)
return m, nil

// 4. RenderFooter() renders the line, blank included — Rule 124 budgets it.
func (m Model) RenderFooter(width int) string {
    return theme.EmptyLineBg(width) + "

}
```

**The expiry carries an id** (`ClearFooterMsg{ID}`): a stale timer does not
clear the message that took its predecessor's place. That is what makes the
type shareable across packages, and it fixes, in passing, a flaw all eight
implementations shared — a message set at t+2.9s was cleared at t+3s by the
previous one's timer.

#### `Status` — what has no timer

A progress indicator, a hint, a loading state: these are **states**, not
events. They are derived on every frame and passed as `View`'s second
argument, never set as a message — a line set when the first repo starts
would be cleared while the tenth is still running.

```go

    if m.loading && len(m.table.Items()) == 0 {
        // the view's own load: the shared dot, with WantsBlink
        return sharedcomponents.Status{Text: "Loading images...", Activity: true}
    }
    // work the router tracks (a run in the registry): the shared dot
    return sharedcomponents.Status{Text: m.progressLine(), Activity: m.anyRunning()}
}
```

Precedence in `View`: **error → warning → info → status**. A failure the
user has not read takes priority over the progress of whatever is still
running.

One field prefixes the line with a mark:

| Field | Mark | Use it for | Driven by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Activity: true` | the shared activity dot, `●` / `○` (same glyph and colour as the row dots, `indicator.Running`) | any loading or running state: work the **router tracks** (a run in the jobs registry) and a view's own load (`WantsBlink()`) | the router's 500 ms blink phase: the view calls `m.footer.SetBlinkPhase(msg.Blink)` from its `jobs.FrameMsg` handler |

`FooterMessage.SetSpinnerFrame`, `theme.SpinnerMessage` and
`theme.SpinnerStyle` no longer exist, and no file under `internal/` may import
`charm.land/bubbles/v2/spinner`. `TestNoViewImportsTheBubblesSpinner` and
`TestRemovedSpinnerSymbolsStayGone` (`internal/app/activity_guard_test.go`)
fail on a reintroduction, with no exception. `dk setup` has no router: it shows
a fixed `●` and the pending text, with no blink. Without a `SetBlinkPhase`
call the dot is steady on. `●` and `○` are one column wide and share a width,
so the phase never shifts the text.

A future `Activity` value that does not depend on the jobs registry must make
its view implement `WantsBlink() bool` (return `status().Activity`, as the
forge explorer does); otherwise the router arms no animation chain and the dot
stays fixed on `●`.

**When a `datatable` is loading, the table stays on screen** and the
loading state is an info message with a mark (the shared activity dot, for the
view's own load as well as for work the router tracks), in the footer only. A body that replaces itself with a loading screen loses its header and columns for the
duration of every `ctrl+r`, then regains them: a layout jump on every
refresh.

**A footer mark is for a table's data loading, never for one row.**
What is happening to a single row (a scan, a clone, a stop) is that row's
activity dot (Rule 125, "The activity column"); when the selected row has a
footer detail with a glyph (`Detail.Glyph`), the footer shows no dot: the
row's own dot already moves.

Mandatory consequence: the empty message ("No images found") is
**conditioned on loading being finished**, otherwise the table announces the
absence of what it is still looking for.

`TestNoTableViewRendersALoadingBody` (`internal/ui/components`) rejects a
loading body in the table views it covers. There is no declared exception.

#### Tests — the timer really does sleep

`tea.Tick` blocks for its entire duration, and `testutil.Msgs` runs the
whole batch it is given: a test that inspects a `Cmd` carrying the timer
pays the full three seconds. The timer starts when the `Cmd` is **built**
(`PostFooter` and `FooterMessage.set` call `tea.Tick` at that moment), not
when it runs: shortening the duration after the `Update` that returned the
`Cmd` is too late, the three seconds are already armed.

- To verify that a message **disappears**, build the expiry rather than
  running the `Cmd`:
  `feed(t, m, components.ClearFooterMsg{ID: m.footer.ID()})`.
- For a test that must drain the `Cmd` (because it is looking for another
  one inside it), shorten the timer **before the `Update` that builds the
  `Cmd`**, as the first line of the test:
  `testutil.FastTimers(t, &components.FooterMsgDuration)`. A helper that
  drains a `Cmd` (like `drive` in `internal/app`) only covers the `Cmds` it
  builds itself.
- `requireNoRealFooterWait(t)` (`internal/app/footer_timer_guard_test.go`)
  fails a test that took over 1.5 s: use it in a test that builds and drains
  footer `Cmds`.

`FooterMsgDuration` is an exported `var` for this reason alone; its
production value is fixed by `TestAMessageGetsThreeSeconds`.

#### Other prohibitions

Mandatory log format: `log.Printf("ERROR [package/view] action: %v", err)`

- ❌ `err.Error()` directly in the UI (except a validation message already
  written to be read)
- ❌ Replacing the view with an error screen (except fatal initialization
  errors)
- ❌ Ignoring an error without `log.Printf`
